• Some of the books written by Bhagat Singh are "Why I Am an Atheist", "No Hanging, Please Shoot Us", and "on the Path of Liberation" among others.​

questions.question: If ‘u’ is the object-distance, ‘v’ is the image-distance and ‘f’ is the focal length of a spherical mirror then which of the following is a correct expression for the mirror formula?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1/v + 1/u = 1/f.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

Spherical Mirror:

__
 
• A spherical mirror is part of a hollow sphere, whose one side is reflecting and the other side is opaque.
 
• Two types of spherical mirrors are:

 
• Concave mirror, whose reflecting surface is towards the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.
 
• Convex mirror, whose reflecting surface is away from the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• Mirror Formula: The following formula is known as the mirror formula, which represents the relation between focal length, image distance, and object distance

Rightarrow (1)/(f)=(1)/(u)+(1)/(v) 

Where, f = focal length, v = the distance of the image from the mirror, and u = the distance of the object from the mirror.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is responsible for sleeping sickness?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protozoa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• African Trypanosomiasis is caused by microscopic parasites (Protozoa) of the species *Trypanosoma **brucei***__.
 
• It is transmitted by the tsetse fly (Glossina species), which is found only in sub-Saharan Africa. It is also known as “**sleeping sickness**”,
 
• __Clinical Features__:- Infection occurs in two stages
 
• __First-stage symptoms__
 __
 
• Headache
 
• Malaise
 
• Weakness
 
• Fatigue
 
• Pruritis
 
 
 
• Second-stage__: The invasion of the central nervous system causes a variety of neuropsychiatric symptoms, such as-
 
 
• Nocturnal insomnia
 
• sudden urges to sleep
 
• hallucinations
 
• delirium
 
• anxiety
 
• emotional lability
 
• attention deficit
 
• motor symptoms (motor weakness, abnormal tone, gait disturbance, ataxia, tremor, speech disturbances).
 
• sensory symptoms (paraesthesia, hyperaesthesia, anesthesia, pruritis, visual problems).

questions.question: The temples of Khajuraho are a magnificent example of the ______ of the temple.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagara style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nagara Style:

 
 
• Nagara's style of temple-making was developed during the Chandela dynasty.
 
• These temples had three chambers namely Garbhagriha, Mandapa and Ardha-mandapa.
 
• Temples are built on relatively high platforms.
 
• Example: Lakshman temple at Khajuraho.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vesara Style:

 
 
• Vesara style of temple making was developed during the Later Chalukya and Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 
• It is a hybridized style of Nagara and Dravidian.
 
• Example: Ladhkhan temple at Aihole.
 
 
 
• Dravidian Style:
 
 
• The Dravidian style of temple-making was developed during the Chola dynasty.
 
• These temples have high boundary walls.
 
• In Dravidian architecture, the main temple has only one vimana and subsidiary shrines do not have vimanas.
 
• Example: Brihadeswara temple at Tanjore.

questions.question: ‘Bhavai’ is the traditional theatre form of which Indian state?

• This form incorporates extensive use of dance to narrate a series of small plays knows as** Vesha or Swanga each with its own plot**.
 
• The word **Bhavai **is derived from the Sanskrit word Bhava, which** means the expression of emotion.**
 
• It is also associated with the Hindu goddess Amba, Bhav means universe and Aai means mother, which means the mother of the universe.
 
• As per the belief, it is started from the** 14th century, Asaita Thakar is traditionally created for its origin.**

questions.question: Manuscripts were usually written on ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**palm leaf.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Manuscripts were usually written on **palm leaf.**
 
• Palm-leaf manuscripts are manuscripts made out of** dried palm leaves**.
 
• Or on the specially prepared **bark of a tree known as the birch,** which grows in the Himalayas, while inscriptions were engraved either on a stone surface or on bricks or metals.
 
• **Birch trees** are usually found in montane forests which are found in high altitude areas.
 
• Birch trees are trees that can grow on the highest altitudes among trees at typically more than** 3500 meters above sea level.**
 
• In India, they can only be seen in the **Himalayan region.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Manuscripts **were written on varied subjects such as religious beliefs and practices, the lives of kings, medicine, and science.
 
• Besides, there were epics, poems, musical dance dramas, and plays. 
 
• Manuscripts are found in hundreds of different languages and scripts.
 
 
• Often, one language is written in a number of different scripts.
 
• For example, Sanskrit is written in Oriya script, Grantha script, Devanagari script, and many other scripts.
 
 

 
• India possesses an estimated five million manuscripts, probably the largest collection in the world.
 
• The **Spitzer Manuscript **is the oldest surviving philosophical manuscript in Sanskrit.
 
• The **oldest manuscript** in the world is** The Pseudo-Apuleius Herbarium, dating back to the 6-7th century.**

questions.question: Which of the following trees is found in mountain forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Cedar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​A **genus of coniferous trees** in the **Pinaceae plant family** is called cedar.
 
• They are native to the** mountains **of the **western Himalayas **and the **Mediterranean region.**
 
• They can be found in the **Mediterranean at 1,000-2,200 m** and at** 1,500-3,200 m** in the **Himalayas.**
 
• Cedrus trees have** broad, level branches, thick, ridged or square-cracked bark, **and a height range between **30 and 40 meters.**
 
• Its wood has a **spicy-resinous aroma.**
 
• The **dimorphic shoots consist of long shoots** that support the branches' framework and **short shoots** that bear the **majority of the leaves.**
 
• The leaves are evergreen, needle-like, **8–60 mm long,** and are grouped in** dense spiral clusters of 15–45 on** short branches and in an** open spiral phyllotaxis** on long shoots.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Trees in** the tropical evergreen forest** include **cinchona, ebony, mahogany, and rosewood.**
 
• Trees in a **tropical deciduous forest** include **oak, maple, birch, beech, aspen, and elm.**
 
• **Acacias, euphorbias, palms, and cacti** are among the vegetation of a** tropical thorn and shrub forest.**
 
• Trees in the **mangrove forest** belong to the genuses **Avicenna, Rhizosphere, Ceriops, and Bruguiera.**
 
• **Rhododendrons, oak, maple, ferns, juniper, and deoder** are the trees found in** montane forests.**

questions.question: Where are villi present in the human alimentary canal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small intestine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alimentary canal**

 
 
• The alimentary canal consists of the mouth, buccal cavity, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, and anus. 
 
 
 
• **Small intestine**
 
 
• The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal.
 
• The small intestine is also the largest part of the alimentary canal.
 
• The small intestine is divided into three regions:
 
• Duodenum (‘C’ shaped)
 
• Jejunum (a long coiled middle portion)
 
• Ileum (highly coiled)
 
• 90 percent of the absorption and digestion occurs in the small intestine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Pancreas**

 
 
• The pancreas functions have both endocrine and exocrine functions.
 
• The pancreas has exocrine glands that produce enzymes that are useful for digestion.
 
• These are released from the acinar cells that act as exocrine cells.
 
• Trypsin, Chymotrypsin is the enzyme secreted by the pancreas that is useful to digest proteins.
 
• The amylase enzyme is useful for the digestion of carbohydrates.
 
• Lipase is used to break down fats.
 
• The endocrine cells are the cells of the Islet of Langerhans which secrete endocrine hormones like insulin and glucagon.
 
 
 
• **Oesophagus**
 
 
• The food pipe through which food is taken to the stomach from the mouth is known as Oesophagus.
 
• Oesophageal cancer starts in the food pipe, also known as your esophagus or gullet.
 
 
 
• **Stomach​**
 
 
• The stomach is a muscular hollow organ.
 
• It takes in food from the esophagus (gullet or food pipe), mixes it, breaks it down, and then passes it on to the small intestine in small portions.
 
• The stomach stores the food for 4-5 hours.
 
• The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the chyme. 
 
• Gastric juice is made up of digestive enzymes, hydrochloric acid, and other substances that are important for absorbing nutrients – about 3 to 4 liters of gastric juice are produced per day.
 
• The hydrochloric acid in the gastric juice breaks down the food and the digestive enzymes split up the proteins.
 
• The acidic gastric juice also kills bacteria.

questions.question: Article 43B was inserted as a _______ in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive principle of state policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 43B**

 
 
• Article 43B deals with the promotion of cooperative societies. 
 
• The State shall endeavor to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies. [Article 43B Inserted by the 97th Constitution Amendment Act, 2011
 
 
 
• **​Directive principle of state policy**
 
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy are stated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It contains Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSPs are non-binding in nature which means they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• These principles emphasize that the State shall try to promote the welfare of the people by providing them with basic facilities like shelter, food, and clothing.
 
• It denotes the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws.
 
• Article 51 is the last Directive Principle of State Policy in the constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional body**

 
 
• Constitutional bodies in India are bodies that are mentioned in the Indian constitution. It derives its power from the Constitution. It can be created or modified only by passing the Constitutional Amendment Bill.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental duty**
 
 
• The Swara n Singh Committee is related to the Fundamental Duties in India.
 
• On the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, 11 Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 51A deals with the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• There are 11 fundamental duties, they are:
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect the national flag & National Anthem.
 
• Follow the ideals of the freedom struggle.
 
• Protect the sovereignty & integrity of India.
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon.
 
• Spirit of a common brotherhood.
 
• Preserve composite culture.
 
• Preserve the natural environment.
 
• Develop a scientific temper.
 
• Safeguard public property.
 
• Strive for excellence.
 
• Duty for all par ents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.
 
 

 
• Fundamental Rights

 
 
• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12-35). Part III of the Constitution is described as the Magna Carta of India.
 
• ‘Magna Carta’, the Charter of Rights issued by King John of England in 1215 was the first written document relating to the Fundamental Rights of citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are justiciable because when violated the aggrieved individual can move the courts for their enforcement.
 
• The Supreme Court or High Courts have the power to issue directions or orders or writs for the enforcement of any of the Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: The Constitution of India states that 'no person shall be eligible for election as President of India unless he has completed the age of ______ years’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**thirty-five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Article 58 : Qualifications for election as President

__
 
• No person shall be eligible for election as President unless he –
 
 
• is a citizen of India;
 
• has completed the age of **thirty-five years**, and
 
• is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People.
 
 
 
• A person shall not be eligible for election as President if he holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State or under any local or other authority subject to the control of any of the said Governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The President is the formal head of the executive, legislature and judiciary of India and is also the commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• He is a part of Union Executive, provisions of which are dealt with Art. 52-78, Part V including Art. related to President (Art. 52-62.)
 
• He is the first citizen of India and acts as the symbol of unity, integrity, and solidarity of the nation.

Article 61 : Procedure for impeachment of the President

 
• When a President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by either House of Parliament.
 
• No such charge shall be preferred unless –
 
 
• the proposal to prefer such charge is contained in a resolution which has been moved after at least fourteen days’ notice in writing signed by not less than one-fourth of the total number of members of the House has been given of their intention to move the resolution, and
 
• such resolution has been passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House.
 
 
 
• When a charge has been so preferred by either House of Parliament, the other House shall investigate the charge or cause the charge to be investigated and the President shall have the right to appear and to be represented at such investigation.
 
• If as a result of the investigation a resolution is passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House by which the charge was investigated or caused to be investigated, declaring that the charge preferred against the President has been sustained, such resolution shall have the effect of removing the President from his office as from the date on which the resolution is so passed.

questions.question: The Tendulkar Committee Report (2011-2012) was based on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**poverty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Tendulkar Expert Group (2009):

__
 
• In 2005, an expert group chaired by Suresh Tendulkar was constituted to review the methodology for poverty estimation.
 
• The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at Rs. 816 per capita per month for rural areas and Rs. 1,000 per capita per month for urban areas.
 
• The Tendulkar poverty line remains the official poverty line and is the basis of the current official poverty estimates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **With respect to the poverty estimation in India:**

Task Force headed by Dr Y. K. Alagh:

 
• This Task Force was constituted in 1977 and it submitted its report in 1979.
 
• Official poverty counts began for the first time in India based on the approach of this Task Force. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• The poverty line was defined as the per capita consumption expenditure level to meet the average per capita daily calorie requirement of 2400 kcal per capita per day in rural areas and 2100 kcal per capita per day in urban areas. 

Rangarajan Committee:

 
• Rangarajan Committee was set up in 2012. This Committee submitted its report in June 2014.
 
• It reverted to the practice of having separate all-India rural and urban poverty line baskets and deriving state-level rural and urban estimates from these. 
 
• This committee raised the daily per capita expenditure to Rs. 47 for urban and Rs. 32 for rural from Rs. 32 and Rs. 26 respectively at 2011-12 prices.
 
• Monthly per capita consumption expenditure of Rs. 972 in rural areas and Rs. 1407 in urban areas is recommended as the poverty line at the all India level.
 
• The government did not take a call on the report of the Rangarajan Committee.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of name of battle and year is/are correctly matched?

I. Battle of Buxar – 1764

II. Battle of Plassey – 1757
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Battle of Buxar:**

 
 
• The battle of Buxar was fought on 22nd October 1764.
 
• This battle was crucial for the Britishers since it provided them with full control of Bengal and Bihar.
 
• It was fought between Hector Munro and the combined forces of Mir Qasim which included Shuja-ud-daula, Shah Alam II, etc.
 
• In this battle, the combined force of Mir Qasim was defeated.
 
• The Treaty of Allahabad was signed on 12 August 1765 between Robert Clive and Shah Alam II (Mughal emperor).
 
• Shah Alam II was forced to pay a fine of five million rupees.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Plassey:**
 
 
• The Battle of Plassey was fought in north-eastern India on 23 June 1757. 
 
• Troops of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, came up against the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.
 
• Clive's victory eventually led to the British becoming the greatest economic and military power in India. 
 
• The Battle of Plassey had political significance for it laid the foundation of the British Empire in India.; it has been rightly regarded as the starting point of British rule in India.
 
• Result of Battle of Plassey-
 
 
• As a result of this victory, Mir Jafar became the Nawab of Bengal. He gave large sums of money plus the zamindari of 24 Parganas to the English.
 
• English rivals, French were ousted.
